stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
In 2022, a regional health department put hand-sanitizer stations at the entrances of two of its four outpatient clinics and left the other two clinics unchanged. Over the next year, officials tracked infections that patients picked up during visits. The department concluded that the stations were linked to fewer infections, because clinics with stations had lower infection rates than clinics without them. For example, ______

Infections Acquired During Clinic Visits, 2022–2023
Clinic | Sanitizer stations | Infections per 1,000 visits
A | Yes | 3.1
B | No | 6.4
C | Yes | 2.8
D | No | 5.9
choices: Clinic A, which had stations, reported 3.1 infections per 1,000 visits, while Clinic C, which also had stations, reported 2.8.
Clinic B, which lacked stations, reported 6.4 infections per 1,000 visits, while Clinic D, which also lacked stations, reported 5.9.
Clinic C, which had stations, reported 2.8 infections per 1,000 visits, while Clinic D, which lacked stations, reported 5.9.
Clinic B, which had stations, reported 6.4 infections per 1,000 visits, while Clinic A, which lacked stations, reported 3.1.
explanation: The sentence has to show that clinics with stations did better than clinics without them, so you need one clinic from each group. Clinic C had stations and 2.8 infections. Clinic D had none and 5.9. That is the difference the department's conclusion depends on.

A.why: You picked a correct reading, but both clinics had stations. Comparing two clinics in the same group can't show that stations made a difference.

B.why: These numbers are right, but both clinics lacked stations. With no clinic that had stations in the comparison, it says nothing about their effect.

D.why: You swapped the rows. The table shows that Clinic B lacked stations and Clinic A had them, so this choice misstates the data.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Every autumn, volunteers at Harrow Ridge count the hawks migrating south along the ridgeline. Ornithologist Dalia Fenn has noticed that one species is passing the site in growing numbers. The volunteers' records back up her observation: at Harrow Ridge, the number of broad-winged hawks counted ______

Autumn Hawk Counts at Harrow Ridge
Year | Broad-winged hawks | Red-tailed hawks
2016 | 4,210 | 1,380
2019 | 5,640 | 1,420
2022 | 7,050 | 1,350
choices: exceeded the number of red-tailed hawks counted in each of the three years shown.
rose from 4,210 in 2016 to 5,640 in 2019 and then to 7,050 in 2022.
fell from 7,050 in 2016 to 5,640 in 2019 and then to 4,210 in 2022.
rose in every single year from 2016 to 2022, reaching 7,050 by the end.
explanation: Fenn's point is that broad-winged hawk numbers are going up, so the sentence needs an increase over time. The counts go from 4,210 to 5,640 to 7,050 across the three years shown, which is exactly that trend.

A.why: This is true, but outnumbering another species isn't the same as increasing. The sentence needs a change over time, not a comparison between species.

C.why: You read the years in reverse. The 4,210 count is from 2016 and the 7,050 count is from 2022, so the numbers went up, not down.

D.why: The table only covers 2016, 2019 and 2022. It can't tell you whether the count rose in every single year in between.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Every flat world map distorts the globe in some way, but map projections distort in different ways and by different amounts. Cartographer Imre Solberg argues that the choice of projection can dramatically change how large high-latitude regions look to a reader. Greenland shows this clearly: ______

Greenland's Displayed Area Relative to Its True Area
Projection | Displayed area ÷ true area
Mercator | 14.0
Robinson | 1.6
Winkel tripel | 1.4
Equal Earth | 1.0
choices: Mercator shows Greenland at 14.0 times its true area, whereas Equal Earth shows it at 1.0 times.
Robinson shows Greenland at 1.6 times its true area, whereas Winkel tripel shows it at 1.4 times.
Equal Earth shows Greenland at 14.0 times its true area, whereas Mercator shows it at 1.0 times.
Winkel tripel shows Greenland at 1.4 times its true area, whereas Equal Earth shows it at 1.0 times.
explanation: Solberg's claim is about a dramatic difference, so you want the two projections that are furthest apart. Mercator enlarges Greenland fourteenfold and Equal Earth shows it at true size. That gap makes the point.

B.why: The values are right, but 1.6 and 1.4 are close together. Two projections that give almost the same result can't show that the choice of projection changes things dramatically.

C.why: You swapped the rows. In the table, Mercator is the one at 14.0 and Equal Earth is the one at 1.0.

D.why: This is an accurate reading, but a gap of 1.4 to 1.0 is small. It doesn't show the dramatic change the sentence calls for.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Fossil pollen trapped in lake sediment shows which plants grew nearby as each layer formed. Paleobotanists studying a sediment core from Lake Varn found that grasses dominated the surrounding landscape during one interval, before forest took over. The share of grass pollen was greatest in the layer dated to ______

Pollen in Lake Varn Sediment Layers
Layer age (years ago) | Grass pollen (%) | Oak pollen (%)
12,000 | 22 | 10
10,000 | 48 | 20
8,000 | 31 | 41
6,000 | 17 | 55
choices: 6,000 years ago, when oak pollen made up 55 percent of the sample.
12,000 years ago, when grass pollen made up 48 percent of the sample.
8,000 years ago, when grass pollen made up 31 percent of the sample.
10,000 years ago, when grass pollen made up 48 percent of the sample.
explanation: The sentence asks for a maximum: the layer where grass pollen was highest. In the grass column, 48 percent is the largest value, and it belongs to the layer dated 10,000 years ago.

A.why: You found a maximum, but it's the oak maximum. The sentence is about grass pollen, and grass was only 17 percent in that layer.

B.why: You paired the right percentage with the wrong row. The 12,000-year layer had 22 percent grass pollen. The 48 percent belongs to the 10,000-year layer.

C.why: This reading is correct, but 31 percent isn't the highest grass value. The sentence needs the greatest share, not just any layer.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Printmakers often choose a technique partly on how many good impressions a plate or block will yield before wear spoils the image. Art historian Lucia Brandt notes that durability varies widely even within a single family of techniques. Among intaglio methods, for instance, ______

Typical Usable Impressions Before Wear
Technique | Family | Usable impressions
Drypoint | Intaglio | 25
Etching | Intaglio | 350
Woodcut | Relief | 1,000
Linocut | Relief | 600
choices: woodcut typically yields about 1,000 usable impressions, while linocut yields about 600.
drypoint typically yields about 25 usable impressions, while etching yields about 350.
drypoint typically yields about 350 usable impressions, while etching yields about 25.
etching typically yields about 350 usable impressions, while woodcut yields about 1,000.
explanation: The key words are "among intaglio methods." You need two intaglio techniques with very different durability. Drypoint and etching are both intaglio, and they yield about 25 and 350 impressions.

A.why: These numbers are right and they do vary, but woodcut and linocut are relief methods. The sentence limits the example to intaglio.

C.why: You swapped the values. In the table, drypoint yields about 25 impressions and etching yields about 350.

D.why: This comparison is accurate, but it crosses two families. Brandt's point is about variation within one family, and woodcut isn't intaglio.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Water that freezes inside concrete expands and can crack a slab. Civil engineers poured two test slabs from the same mix, cured them the same way, and made one change: Slab 2 contained an air-entraining additive, which leaves tiny bubbles where freezing water can expand. The engineers expected the additive to reduce cracking. The results matched that expectation: after 300 freeze-thaw cycles, ______

Surface Cracks After Freeze-Thaw Cycles
Slab | Additive | Cracks after 100 cycles | Cracks after 300 cycles
1 | No | 4 | 19
2 | Yes | 1 | 3
choices: Slab 2, which had the additive, showed 3 cracks, compared with 19 for Slab 1, which did not.
Slab 1, which lacked the additive, went from 4 cracks at 100 cycles to 19 at 300 cycles.
Slab 1, which had the additive, showed 3 cracks, compared with 19 for Slab 2, which did not.
Slab 2, which had the additive, went from 1 crack at 100 cycles to 3 at 300 cycles.
explanation: The only difference between the slabs is the additive, so the sentence has to compare the two slabs at 300 cycles. Slab 2, with the additive, had 3 cracks and Slab 1 had 19. The additive reduced cracking.

B.why: This reading is correct, but it only tracks one slab over time. Without the other slab in the comparison, it can't show what the additive did.

C.why: You mixed up the slabs. The passage and the table both say Slab 2 had the additive, not Slab 1.

D.why: This is accurate, but it only shows Slab 2 getting worse over time. It leaves out the slab without the additive, so it can't show the additive's effect.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Ecologists surveying three meadows expected that mowing once a year would sharply reduce the number of bee species a meadow supports. The survey did not bear this out. For bees, the unmowed meadow and the meadow mowed once a year were nearly identical: ______

Pollinator Species Recorded in Three Meadows
Meadow | Management | Bee species | Butterfly species
North | Unmowed | 41 | 18
South | Mowed once yearly | 39 | 9
East | Mowed monthly | 22 | 6
choices: the unmowed North meadow had 18 butterfly species, and the once-mowed South meadow had 9.
the once-mowed South meadow had 39 bee species, and the monthly-mowed East meadow had 22.
the unmowed North meadow had 41 bee species, and the once-mowed South meadow had 39.
the unmowed North meadow had 22 bee species, and the once-mowed South meadow had 39.
explanation: The sentence needs a similarity, and it's about bees in the unmowed and once-mowed meadows. North had 41 bee species and South had 39. The numbers are nearly identical, as the sentence says.

A.why: You compared the right meadows but used the butterfly column. Those numbers also show a big gap, not a similarity.

B.why: These numbers are right, but East is the meadow mowed monthly, not the unmowed one. The comparison also shows a large difference.

D.why: You misread North's bee count. The 22 belongs to East. North had 41.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Seismic waves generally weaken as they travel away from an earthquake's epicenter, but the ground beneath a site also matters. Seismologist Farah Okonjo claims that loose sediment amplifies shaking compared with solid bedrock. Readings from two stations almost the same distance from a recent quake support her claim: ______

Peak Ground Acceleration at Four Stations
Station | Ground type | Distance from epicenter (km) | Peak acceleration (g)
Aldo | Bedrock | 30 | 0.08
Bexley | Sediment | 31 | 0.21
Corran | Bedrock | 62 | 0.04
Dunmore | Sediment | 90 | 0.07
choices: Aldo, on bedrock, recorded 0.08 g, while Corran, also on bedrock, recorded 0.04 g.
Bexley, on bedrock, recorded 0.21 g, while Aldo, on sediment, recorded 0.08 g.
Dunmore, on sediment, recorded 0.07 g, while Aldo, on bedrock, recorded 0.08 g.
Bexley, on sediment, recorded 0.21 g, while Aldo, on bedrock, recorded 0.08 g.
explanation: You need two stations at almost the same distance on different ground, with the sediment station shaking harder. Bexley (sediment, 31 km) recorded 0.21 g and Aldo (bedrock, 30 km) recorded 0.08 g.

A.why: The values are right, but both stations are on bedrock and they are at different distances. This comparison can't show anything about sediment.

B.why: You swapped the ground types. The table shows Bexley on sediment and Aldo on bedrock.

C.why: This is accurate, but Dunmore is three times as far from the epicenter as Aldo, and the sediment station shook less. It doesn't show amplification.
